title_en: China & the shifting investment leadership in Asia 9/21/26
title_zh: 中国与亚洲投资主导权的转移 | Brendan Ahern（CraneShares）、Andrew Mattock（Matthews）
subtitle_zh: 特朗普与习近平会晤背景下，中美投资逻辑与 AI 供应链的再定价。
description: China & the shifting investment leadership in Asia 9/21/26

turns.en: The ETF Edge podcast is sponsored by Invesco QQQ. Let's rethink possibility. Invesco Distributors Inc. Welcome to ETF Edge, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange-traded funds, you're in the right place.
turns.zh: 《ETF Edge》播客由 Invesco QQQ 赞助播出。让我们重新思考无限可能。Invesco Distributors Inc. 出品。欢迎收听《ETF Edge》播客——如果你想了解关于交易所交易基金（ETF）的一切最新洞见，那你来对地方了。

turns.en: Every week, we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis, and breaking down what it all means for investors. I'm your host, Dominic Chu.
turns.zh: 每周我们都会带来精彩的访谈、深入的市场分析，并为你拆解这一切对投资者意味着什么。我是主持人 Dominic Chu。

turns.en: President Trump and Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, are getting together this week for a state-oriented meeting and looking to revive some economic relations as well.
turns.zh: 特朗普总统与中国领导人习近平本周将举行一场国事访问级别的会晤，双方也希望能借此重启一部分经济关系。

turns.en: Here is my conversation with Brendan Ahern, the chief investment officer at Crane Shares, alongside Andrew Mattock, portfolio manager at Matthews.
turns.zh: 以下是我与 CraneShares 首席投资官 Brendan Ahern，以及 Matthews 组合基金经理 Andrew Mattock 的对谈。

turns.en: Gentlemen, thank you very much for being with us here on ETF Edge. I wanted to kind of put that in context in the introduction because the reason why there's a lot of attention being paid to the Chinese versus US investment thesis is because Trump and Xi will meet later on this week.
turns.zh: 二位，非常感谢你们来到《ETF Edge》。我之所以在开场做这个铺垫，是因为现在大家对中国 vs 美国的投资逻辑关注度很高，原因就在于特朗普和习近平本周晚些时候将要会晤。

turns.en: And maybe I'll start from a big-picture point of view, Brendan, with you. Just how important is this particular meeting towards maybe, I don't want to say resetting, but maybe setting the stage for the next leg of our relationship with China?
turns.zh: 我想先从大局观开始问你，Brendan。这次会晤到底有多重要——我不想用"重置"这个词，但它会不会为我们与中国关系的下一阶段定下基调？

turns.en: Well, that's exactly how we see it, Dom, that this is a re-rating of US-China relations. President Trump as a business person, I think is very attuned to US corporate interests.
turns.zh: 我们的看法正是如此，Dom——这是一次中美关系的重新定价（re-rating）。特朗普总统作为商人，我认为他对美国企业的利益非常敏锐。

turns.en: US Congress just reported that US companies generate half a trillion of revenue in China annually. And so I think this is an opportunity for kind of this re-rating stabilization of the relationship really driven by maybe partnerships from US and Chinese corporations.
turns.zh: 美国国会刚刚报告说，美国企业每年在中国创造五千亿美元的营收。所以我认为这是一个机会——关系的重新定价与企稳，实际上可能由中美企业的合作伙伴关系来推动。

turns.en: How much have you sensed, by the way, over the course of not just the first Trump administration, but into this one as well, how much of the US investor base has had some kind of influence or effect based upon the predominantly trading relationship that we have with China and the rhetoric that has gone along with it since 2016 at this point?
turns.zh: 顺便问一下，不只是第一届特朗普政府，也包括这一届——你感受到美国投资者群体在多大程度上受到了中美这种以贸易为主的关系的影响？以及 2016 年以来一直伴随其左右的那些政治修辞带来的效应？

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. I think that rhetoric, that geopolitical rhetoric has really weighed on US investor sediment. At the same time, that's not necessarily true outside of the US, where particularly the commodity world is so geared to China that they kind of have to do business there, and their institutions are very geared.
turns.zh: 对，没错。我认为这些地缘政治修辞确实压制了美国投资者的情绪。但与此同时，在美国之外就不一定了——尤其大宗商品领域高度依赖中国，它们基本上不得不在那边做生意，其机构配置也非常侧重于中国。

turns.en: Understand that here in the US, we've had this incredible bull market, so I think it's just been a little out of sight, out of mind because of a little bit of this geopolitics, and that's where we're more constructive that this stabilization would allow US investors to come back into the space.
turns.zh: 要知道在美国这边，我们经历了一轮非常强劲的牛市，所以我觉得因为这点地缘政治，中国基本就是眼不见心不烦。而我们更乐观的地方在于——这种企稳会让美国投资者重新回到这个领域。

turns.en: All right, so Andrew, interesting point being made here with regard to our relationship there. From an investor standpoint, have you seen over the course of, say, that 10-year span?
turns.zh: 好，Andrew，这里就我们和中国的关系提出了一个很有意思的观点。从投资者角度看，在过去大约十年这个跨度里，你有没有感受到变化？

turns.en: I know it's a big kind of time window to look at, but at Matthew's, you have been investing in Asian equities more broadly, and even specifically in China, for even longer than that.
turns.zh: 我知道这个时间窗口挺大的，但你们在 Matthews 做亚洲股票已经很久了，专注中国的时间甚至更早。

turns.en: How much has the investing landscape, in terms of sentiment, shifted over the course of the past 10 years, given this kind of US and China predominantly trade relationship but now extending to things like AI as well?
turns.zh: 过去十年里，在中美这种以贸易为主、如今又延伸到 AI 等领域的关系背景下，投资格局在情绪层面发生了多大的变化？

turns.en: Yeah, it's been up and down. You know, the low point was probably just two years ago where we had that sort of big spat, really, and we've come a long way since then.
turns.zh: 确实起伏很大。低点大概在两年前，那时候真的是相当大的摩擦，从那以后我们已经走了很长的路。

turns.en: You know, the dialogue, Scott Bassent yesterday had some positive things to say. You know, anything we hear, you know, like that from a Chinese equity point of view, does alleviate a lot of concerns that people had even two years ago, let alone 10 years ago.
turns.zh: 你知道的，对话方面，Scott Bessent 昨天说了一些积极的话。从中国股票的角度看，任何这样的积极信号，都能缓解人们两年前甚至十年前的很多担忧。

turns.en: On the same time, you know, China's going through its own domestic issues that it's getting over the top of, particularly the property market.
turns.zh: 与此同时，中国自身也在处理国内的难题，而且正在逐步走出困境，尤其是房地产市场。

turns.en: So that's also in the background, but it's great to see from an investor's point of view that some of this external noise is starting to dissipate.
turns.zh: 所以这也存在于背景之中，但从投资者角度看，外部这些噪音开始消散，确实是一件好事。

turns.en: Andrew, from that portfolio manager's point of view, just where have you started to see a little bit more of the pickup and activity with regard to the types of companies and the types of markets that investors are kind of shifting more of their attention towards?
turns.zh: Andrew，从组合经理的角度看，你在哪些类型的公司、哪些市场上开始看到投资者活动增多、关注度提升？

turns.en: If they are investing in Asian markets or want to invest more internationally, globally, XUS, how exactly are they viewing that and what exactly are they looking at with regard to the types of investments?
turns.zh: 如果他们投亚洲市场，或者想在除美国以外（XUS）的更大范围做全球配置，他们具体是怎么看待的？关注哪些类型的投资？

turns.en: Is it strictly tech in Asia-related or is it go beyond that? Yeah, so, you know, let's start with China and then we'll broaden that out. You know, what we're seeing is quite narrow, very AI focused, a lot more sort of Shanghai, Shenzhen, listed stocks, very technology heavy.
turns.zh: 是纯粹的亚洲科技，还是超越科技？好，先从中国说起，然后再往外拓宽。我们看到的是相当集中的——非常聚焦 AI，上海、深圳上市的股票比较多，科技含量很重。

turns.en: What we're seeing though from an earnings perspective in China is earnings broadening out. So, you know, materials was mentioned, financials, healthcare.
turns.zh: 不过从盈利角度看，中国的盈利正在向更多板块扩散。你之前提到的材料，还有金融、医疗都是。

turns.en: So we're starting to see sort of signs of life in other places from an earnings perspective and investors are paying attention. The one soggy point still is really the consumer, both the discretionary and staples.
turns.zh: 所以我们开始在其它板块从盈利角度看到一些生机，投资者也在关注。唯一依然疲软的还是消费，无论是可选消费还是必需消费。

turns.en: Now, broadening that out to the rest of Asia, you know, the indices really tell it all. You know, Taiwan and Korea, when you look at the makeup of the emerging market, indices at the moment dominate and that's really been driven by, you know, the AI boom in the US and that filtering through to Asian supply chains.
turns.zh: 把视野扩到亚洲其它地方，指数真的说明了一切。你看台湾和韩国，在新兴市场指数中的构成里目前占主导，而这背后其实是美国的 AI 热潮传导到亚洲供应链的结果。

turns.en: But there are opportunities outside of that starting to appear. I mentioned a few in China, you know, India sort of gone off the radar screen as well.
turns.zh: 但 AI 之外的机会也开始显现。我在中国提到了一些，而印度则差不多从雷达上消失了。

turns.en: So, you know, outside of AI, things are starting to broaden out, but I wouldn't say that it's, you know, it's still heavily focused in on that AI story.
turns.zh: 所以，AI 之外的东西确实在开始扩散，但我不会说它已经分散开了——目前主要还是高度聚焦在 AI 这条主线上。

turns.en: So, Brendan, it's a great point because Andrew brought up an interesting discussion about the difference between mainland China investing versus investing offshore in Hong Kong.
turns.zh: Brendan，这是个很好的切入点，因为 Andrew 提到了一个很有意思的话题——投资中国内地与投资离岸港股之间的差别。

turns.en: Now, I mean, it's nuanced, but it's important, right? It is still the Asian market and Hong Kong is technically part of China, but the way that those companies that list in those different markets and the types of companies that are there are also very different in the way that those markets are treated.
turns.zh: 这里面有微妙之处，但很重要，对吧？它们都是亚洲市场，香港从技术上讲也是中国的一部分，但在不同市场上市的公司、公司类型都很不一样，这些市场受到的待遇也很不同。

turns.en: So, how exactly are investors treating that relationship? If I was to invest in a broad-based China ETF, most of that these days is gonna be in Hong Kong listed shares of some of the biggest tech and financial companies that we know out there internationally.
turns.zh: 那投资者到底是怎么看待这种关系的？如果我买一只宽基中国 ETF，现在大部分仓位其实是那些我们国际上熟知的大型科技和金融公司在港股上市的股份。

turns.en: But it's different when you start going into the Shanghai Shenzhen markets, which are much more locally focused and with names that we don't necessarily view as brand names, if there are such a thing for us in the U.S., vis-a-vis China.
turns.zh: 但当你开始进入沪深市场就不一样了——那边更偏本地化，很多名字对我们来说根本算不上什么品牌——如果站在美国对中国的视角来看的话。

turns.en: Yeah, 100%, I think this is where all ETFs are really driven by an underlying index, and I think that's where this is very key that in the case of China, that definition of China is 80% Hong Kong, 5% U.S. ADRs.
turns.zh: 对，完全同意。我认为所有 ETF 本质上都是由底层指数驱动的，而关键在于——就中国而言，"中国"这个定义是 80% 港股、5% 美国存托凭证（ADR）。

turns.en: If you look at the big companies in that Hong Kong market, you have banks, financials, but you also have a lot of discretionary names, and to Andrew's point, you have a housing situation that's weighed on the consumer, so those earnings per share growth has been very poor.
turns.zh: 你看港股里的大公司，有银行、金融，也有很多可选消费标的；就像 Andrew 说的，房地产的问题拖累了消费，所以那些公司的每股收益（EPS）增长非常疲软。

turns.en: Conversely, 15%, which is basically non-existent for global professional investors, even bother to look at the Shanghai Shenzhen, you have things like the Starboard, where the Science and Technology Board is where all of the Chinese semiconductor stocks like CXMT have listed a company that called Enflame recently listed, Unitry, the big robotics, the largest robotics maker globally, and those companies are benefiting
turns.zh: 反过来看那 15%——对全球专业投资者来说几乎等于不存在，很少有人去关注沪深市场。但那里有科创板（Science and Technology Board），所有中国的半导体公司都在那里上市，比如长鑫存储（CXMT）已经上市，摩尔线程（Enflame）最近也上了，还有宇树（Unitree），全球最大的机器人制造商。这些公司正在受益于

turns.en: from the AI hyperscalers spending, right? That capex is ending up the balance sheets of these Starboard listed companies similar to Korea, Taiwan, and Japan, so this is a little bit of a nuanced situation where Hong Kong hasn't seen that earnings per share growth.
turns.zh: AI 超大规模玩家（hyperscalers）的支出，对吧？那些资本开支（capex）最终落到了这些科创板公司的资产负债表上，跟韩国、台湾、日本的情况类似。所以这是个有点微妙的局面——港股没有看到那种每股收益的增长。

turns.en: Investors are gravitating to those four markets, but again, a little bit out of sight, out of mind, because you gotta really dig in and find those Shanghai listed Science and Technology Board names that we hold in our K-Star ETF.
turns.zh: 投资者正流向这四个市场，但同样还是眼不见心不烦，因为你得真正深挖，才能找到那些在上交所科创板上市的公司——也就是我们 K-Star ETF 里持有的那些。

turns.en: You know, it's interesting, Andrew, because that's what your job is, right? Your job is to sit there and dig through all of these things to try to find those names that are not necessarily, and again, I'm only using it because we here in the US and even internationally, ex-China and ex-Hong Kong, we tend to think of the brand names that go into Chinese investing.
turns.zh: 很有意思，Andrew，因为这恰恰是你的工作，对吧？你的职责就是坐在那里把这些东西翻个底朝天，去找到那些未必知名的名字。我之所以这么说是因为——我们美国和全球的投资者，抛开中国和港股不谈，提到中国投资往往想到的都是那些品牌名。

turns.en: When you look at the big ADRs that trade here, or the big ETFs that hold holdings that are based in Hong Kong, we're talking about names like Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, the ones that have become more synonymous with the Chinese tech trade over the years, but it's very different these days.
turns.zh: 当你看这里交易的大型 ADR，或者持有港股的大型 ETF，说的都是 Alibaba、Tencent、Baidu 这样的名字——多年来它们几乎成了中国科技交易的代名词。但现在很不一样了。

turns.en: Specifically, I would say just in the last year, maybe even six to nine months, because many of the names that we are talking about that are not brand name yet, but are getting a lot more attention, are Chinese AI names that are not those ones that I mentioned before.
turns.zh: 我尤其想说就在最近一年，甚至六七个月到九个月以来——因为很多我们讨论的名字虽然还不是大品牌，却受到了越来越多的关注，它们是中国 AI 公司，而不是我之前提到的那几家。

turns.en: So how exactly do you go about doing that kind of bottoms up stock picking for that earnings growth, for that revenue picture, and what exactly makes a good investment in China if it's not gonna be in their equivalent of what we would call hyperscalers?
turns.zh: 那你们到底是怎么做这种自下而上（bottoms up）的选股的？去看盈利增长、看营收前景？如果投的不是他们的"超大规模玩家"对标者，那到底什么样的中国投资才算是一笔好投资？

turns.en: Yeah, so some very good points there, but just to pick up there, the mainland market Shanghai, Shenzhen, which aren't included to any large degree in most of these global indices.
turns.zh: 对，你提出了很多很好的观点，但我接着往下说——内地市场，沪深，在绝大多数全球指数里根本没有被大规模纳入。

turns.en: I mean, this is the second biggest stock market in the world, and it's not included. So it's up to us, and hence the Mathis China Fund. We have the Mathis China Innovation Fund as well.
turns.zh: 要知道这是全球第二大股票市场，却不在指数里。所以这就得靠我们了——这也是 Matthews China Fund 的由来，我们还有 Matthews China Innovation Fund。

turns.en: To go through these companies, it's a very deep, it's a very liquid, it's a very interesting place. Now, we're talking about AI, and we're talking about IT, but it's very interesting in lots of other places as well.
turns.zh: 去逐一研究这些公司——这是一个非常深、流动性非常好、也非常有趣的市场。我们现在聊的是 AI 和 IT，但很多其它领域同样很有意思。

turns.en: And to your point, just not included in most of these global indices. So that's where, you know, it's up to us to step into that role and fill in the pieces.
turns.zh: 就像你说的，它们没有被纳入大多数全球指数。所以这正是我们该顶上去、把缺口补上的地方。

turns.en: How exactly then do you figure out what those pieces are? If I could follow up with that, Andrew, how exactly do you then pick the types of companies that go into a broader portfolio for your clients?
turns.zh: 那你们具体是怎么搞清楚这些缺口在哪里的？我想追问一下，Andrew——你怎么挑选放进客户更宽泛组合里的那些公司？

turns.en: So Mathis Asia, you know, we go back a long time, 25 years plus. So the level and the depth of experience we have, and it's not just in China, and it's not, you know, we have the China Fund, China Innovation Fund, we also have the Korea Fund.
turns.zh: Matthews Asia 有很长的历史了，25 年以上。我们在这些市场上的经验广度和深度都很强，而且不只是中国——我们有 China Fund、China Innovation Fund，还有 Korea Fund。

turns.en: You know, emerging market funds. So lots of experience across the board in lots of these markets, but particularly in China, because China is a big part of all these, even these broader funds.
turns.zh: 还有新兴市场基金。所以在很多市场上都有丰富经验，但尤其在中国，因为即便是这些更宽泛的基金，中国也是一大块。

turns.en: Getting on the ground at guys in Hong Kong, you know, it's all really part of the process that we go through to try and to pick out the, you know, the nuggets, if you like, for what is a very, very, very deep market.
turns.zh: 让团队在港股实地调研——这些都是我们整套流程的一部分，就是为了从一个非常非常深的市场里，把那些真金白银挑出来。

turns.en: Brendan, from an ETF investor perspective, there are a lot of folks who now will look at these investments. I'm using K-Web as an example, because it just seems to be one of the more well-known ETFs out there, KWEB for the China Internet ETF.
turns.zh: Brendan，从 ETF 投资者的角度看，现在有很多人会关注这些投资。我拿 KWEB 举例，因为它可能是最知名的中国 ETF 之一——就是那只中国互联网 ETF。

turns.en: The names that are in there for the most part, the ones that are the most heavily weighted, are the ones I mentioned before, the ones that we all kind of have grown up around for the past 10, 15 years.
turns.zh: 里面大部分仓位、权重最高的，就是我之前提到的那些——过去十年、十五年我们已经耳熟能详的名字。

turns.en: But a lot more the story, just like here these days, is being driven around some of these smaller or even private companies that are making bigger strides and showing some of that higher growth, versus say a meta-platforms or an Apple or an Alphabet or anything of that like.
turns.zh: 但现在越来越多的故事，就像这里一样，是由一些更小的、甚至私有的公司在驱动，它们进步更大、增速更高，而不是那些超大型平台、Apple、Alphabet 之类的。

turns.en: How then do investors go about expressing that view through ETFs as opposed to fundamental research on their own for trying to invest in these types of companies?
turns.zh: 那投资者如何通过 ETF 来表达这个观点，而不是靠自己做基本面研究去投这些公司？

turns.en: And I say that because many of the types of companies that we're reading about are not really generally all that accessible for investors here in the United States, as opposed to those ETF managers with boots on the ground, so to speak, who can access those markets in a better way.
turns.zh: 我之所以这么问，是因为我们读到的很多这类公司，对美国投资者来说其实并没有那么容易买到，反倒是那些有实地团队的 ETF 管理人能更好地接入这些市场。

turns.en: I mean, I think that's really the point of an ETF is to do something for you that you can't or really don't want to do on your own. And when you invest in KWEB, we're going out and converting your US dollars into Hong Kong dollars and buying these underlying stocks on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
turns.zh: 我觉得这就是 ETF 的真正意义——帮你做到你自己做不到、或者根本不想做的事。当你买 KWEB，其实就是我们替你美元换成港币，去港交所买入这些底层股票。

turns.en: Yes, you're getting exposure to the big companies like an Alibaba and a Tencent that have ADRs here. At the same time, the liquidity in Hong Kong is much, much deeper than here in the US.
turns.zh: 对，你获得了对 Alibaba、Tencent 这类大公司（它们在这里有 ADR）的敞口；同时，港股的流动性比美国这边深得多。

turns.en: And also, we are giving you exposure to some of the AI large language models, companies like ZAI and Minimax that went public earlier this year, that you're getting a little bit of Lenovo, which is kind of benefiting from the picks and shovels trade that's really benefited the Korea and Taiwan and Japan as well.
turns.zh: 而且，我们也给了你一些 AI 大模型公司的敞口，比如今年早些时候上市的 Z.ai 和 MiniMax；还有一点 Lenovo——它受益于"卖铲人"（picks and shovels）逻辑，这个逻辑同样利好了韩国、台湾和日本。

turns.en: So you are getting some exposure. I just think you've had this really strong 17-year US bull market. Yes, throw on some of the geopolitics, some of the consumption issues in China.
